observation: A single dark 3 with two curved lobes; no punctuation or underline.

The opening short adjective is visibly abbreviated/contracted; it is not expanded. A long horizontal cancellation crosses the old central line. Topologie sur and the serif I are plausible beneath it; the following mathematical mark cannot be recovered, while a phi-like loop remains. The raised l'application and underlined surjection are legible. The smaller words above surjection and the far-right replacement remain uncertain. At far right the lower old word is crossed but unreadable. The mathematical line along the lower edge belongs to the next box.

The crossed left phrase is only partly recoverable. The first parameter is a capital J form; the later j descends below its parenthesis. Separate bars occur over J/j and over the full right inverse-image expressions. Two pairs of short vertical equality strokes attach the union annotations below the first equality. The first lower union bound has a visible short bar over J; the other two have plain J. The lower annotation is close to the crop edge but its stars, equals sign and union bounds remain visible.

The raised loc finie has a short underline and a separate curved attachment leader; no independent stop after loc is secure there. The line under préordonné begins after the prefix. The map has one rightward head. The word after the map is compressed and retains application/surjection uncertainty. The cancelled short word before les is darkened by its strike. The union lower bound has an angle with a lower equality bar. The later loc. has a visible stop; stars occur on the family entries and in the parenthesis, not on the left X_i.

The leading numeral is overworked. Top. and finale are legible; the small parenthetical clause after que remains partly unreadable, with a quantifier-like glyph and two small index-like bodies retained uncertain. The far-right upper connector has a clear left head but no distinct right head. The lower middle connector is double-lined, but its left end is less clear than its right. The open-set letter has a cup/angle form that does not securely distinguish U from L. Both X entries carry raised stars.

Rotated 22 degrees clockwise for the marginal line. The arrow has two parallel upward shafts and an upper head. Surj. ends in a descending j and separate stop. The small number after i.e. is overworked and remains uncertain. The large partial 3 at lower right is neighbouring main-text numbering, not another marginal number.

The left subscript and the quantified letter both have a detached dot and a pronounced left-hooked lower foot, leaving i/j uncertain. The union bound reads j less-than-or-equal i and has a separate short underline beneath its first portion. A separate bar spans the left X/star. The number 3°) is clear. The NB text at lower right is neighbouring context for a later box.

The number 1°) is clear. Surj has no secure independent terminal stop before i.e. The nonempty-set glyph is a small loop crossed by a long sloping shaft, retained as phi-shaped ink. The raised star touches the upper crop edge. Two separate parallel oblique rule ends are visible at lower left; they are recorded as two rules without assigning them as an underline of the numeral.

NB has one separate underline and no secure following stop. The second numbered condition is hooked/overworked and remains uncertain. A detached oblique bar lies above the serif I. The word before d'inclusion begins rel- but its compressed ending does not justify expansion. The long lower horizontal stroke is positioned over the final X/star group and is retained as its bar, not as an underline of the preceding text. Three terminal points follow that group.

The first word is retraced but supports Une. The formula has a raised star. The line-start sign on the next line is two separate horizontal strokes, followed by a two-point colon. D'une and the abbreviation d'équiv. are retained literally. A small raised ending after loc is t-like but not fully separate; the following underline extends through finie. The underline under ouverte has a curved right ending. The lower cancelled-line fragments are outside this target passage.

A continuous heavy strike crosses the entire lower phrase. Telle que les is recoverable. The following long word has two tall early strokes and a later tall t-like body; éléments is preferred, but the strike masks the middle joins. The final looped d/e group reaches the upper crop boundary. Fragments from the live line above are excluded.

The end of quotient is compressed/abbreviated and is not resolved by expansion. A sloping insertion attachment occurs before ordre; the raised pré is clipped at this box's upper boundary but partly present in the preceding supplied context. Two horizontal cancellation strokes obscure the intervening old phrase, which cannot be recovered word by word. The short live word before I remains uncertain. Ordonné has a distinct underline; the final short group is ssi.

The opening quantifier/parenthesis region is clipped at the left and is not completed. Both left X/star groups have separate bars. The X_i in the right parenthesis has no visible star. The first connector is a double rightward implication; the second has heads at both ends. The abbreviation loc. and terminal stop are visible.

The marginal ordonné is underlined. The vertical double-line connector has heads at both top and bottom. The two heading words have separate underline strokes. Croissante is raised with a continuous curved leader to the family phrase, so that leader is not treated as a separate underline. The order comparison is a simple less-than angle. The prose containment phrase is compressed and remains uncertain. Both bars in the union bound are separate strokes over i and j. No stars occur on the family X entries in this passage.

The first article has a small loop without a secure l ascender. Pour is raised at the left with a curved leader before Toute. The word modérées near the end of the second line has an underline. Partition is visibly crossed and stratification is written above it; the following raised words are crowded and remain uncertain. The long cancellation extends through the region of fine telle, but its exact scope relative to their low bodies is uncertain. The last cancelled word has a long p/f-like descender and obscured joins. No grammatical restoration is imposed on the revised sentence.
The central numeral has the diagonal, crossbar and descending shaft of 4. A long curved stroke lies to its right and turns left below it; no independent left parenthesis is secure within this box.

This marginal formula runs opposite the main text; the same crop was reoriented to 180 degrees. The first two large serif letters have hooked lower strokes, favouring J but leaving I possible; the first has a separate bar. A vertical separator follows them. Above y the crossed membership and J are vertically stacked; above x membership and J share a line. The final x-in-J group is separate. No arrowhead is added to the separator.

Partition indexée is raised above the cancelled opening noun; de X is also raised farther right. Two long cancellation strokes cross the older description and its continuation. The noun and small group before the final map cannot be recovered completely. The map shaft coincides with the cancellation, so its arrow status remains uncertain. The opening X has a small angular raised mark whose exact star/prime form is not secure. Cond. and the following colon remain outside the strike.

The small opening label is clipped and unresolved. The upper long strike crosses almost all text after the quantifier; que/on, the parenthetical phrase and the final mathematical cluster cannot be recovered fully. The nonempty sign has a diagonal slash, and the following empty-set-shaped glyph is a loop with a long crossing shaft. The lower X/star has a separate bar and is not crossed; est is also outside the lower strike. The lower cancellation starts around the following word, whose joining strokes remain partly obscured. Its later X subscript is crossed.

The small black sign immediately after the existential quantifier is overworked; a less-than-or-equal form is only a candidate. Relation has a continuous cancellation across it. Pré is raised above ordre with a curved attachment. The serif I has a detached upper horizontal stroke but its relation to the letter's roof is not fully secure in this compressed crop. The final quantifier and two index letters reach the right edge. Lower-line fragments are excluded.

The upper formula and crossed parenthesis are clipped by the top edge; the proposed bar on its initial X is therefore uncertain. Its union bound has a visible bar over i. In the lower line the order sign has a lower equality bar, both inverse connectors have two heads, and the containment signs have no equality strokes. Separate bars span the first two X/star groups and the last X/star group; the X immediately after the parenthetical equivalence has no bar. The large dark closing-shaped mark after the second barred X is overworked and remains locally unresolved.

The old sa relation phrase is crossed by one continuous line; its final word remains partly hidden. Préordre after the strike is live. The short words following it are faint and compressed. The final word is visibly abbreviated, with a long p descender and a separate stop, rather than a fully written topologie. A comma-like descending mark follows. The serif I shows one upper horizontal cap; no independent second bar is secure here.

The opening criterion and loc with raised t are legible. The phrase around the cancelled lower-left word and its replacement is heavily crowded; neither the deleted candidate stricte nor stratification is secure letter by letter. A curved descending leader attaches the lower explanatory text. Its visible loc. finie and later disjoints are retained, while intervening text and attachment remain uncertain. The right and lower boundaries clip the explanatory continuation; no closing parenthesis or missing predicate is supplied. The next-line 1-1 phrase is excluded here.

The word correspondance is above a densely crossed old group, which cannot be recovered. The 1-1 line runs along the upper crop boundary and is read only where present. The central relations d'équivalence and lower finies et ouvertes are legible. The small raised sur X group is followed by compressed letters and a long curved attachment; its proposed fermées and exact placement remain uncertain. The short connective before des familles is likewise unresolved. The closing parenthesis after à iso près is visible. The vertical left rule and stratification fragments belong to neighbouring material.

The family entries have no stars. The ending of indexées/indexés is compressed. Ordonné, the raised loc. finie, croissante and recouvrant each have a separate underline. The old word before the inserted fermées is obliterated by several close strokes; its wording cannot be recovered. The tiny black group between de X and recouvrant is unresolved, with et only a candidate. The first and second numbered conditions are both visible; the next formula continues beyond this box. The serif I forms each show one cap.

The inserted word has a tall descending f, low er-m joins and a detached acute accent over the ending. A long stroke beneath it begins in a loop/return at the left and may be its attachment leader rather than an independent underline; that state remains explicit. The tall left rule and lower formula fragments are neighbouring context.

The intersection formula has two separate bars in the union bound. The fourth condition has a crossed mathematical cluster after its numeral, with X_k preferred but the old strokes not fully separable. The implication has a right head. Rare and dans have distinct underline strokes. The following parenthetical equality has a bar over the first X/star only. The inserted third condition is enclosed/attached by a broad curved leader; this is not counted as punctuation or deletion. Its small definition is written below X_i-star with paired vertical equality strokes and déf. The empty-set-shaped glyph is a loop with a long crossing shaft. The Moyennant line at the bottom is next-paragraph context.

The slanted marginal note was rotated clockwise in its single saved crop. NB has a separate underline. The conditions read 1, 2 and 4, followed by 3 as the subject of équivaut. The short cond. is retained without expansion; a short horizontal stroke below it may be an underline or a joining/attachment stroke. The final X_i has no visible star. Its inequality has a crossing slash and the following glyph is phi-shaped. The long oblique page rule and the large arrow/main-formula fragments crossing the crop are not treated as cancellation or as part of this note. No terminal stop is secure.

A partly clipped star-like marginal marker precedes Moyennant. Both cited condition numbers have closing parentheses. The defining formula has a star on the left X and on the X under the union; the middle X_i is unstarred, and the union bound is a plain less-than sign. The p. before partition is retained as an abbreviation. Loc. finie is raised with a curved leader to partition. The short word before conditions remains uncertain. The small text along the lower crop boundary is continuation/context and is not completed here.

The three principal words have separate underline strokes. The middle adjective has a tall f and several compressed following joins, favouring stratifiante but leaving stratifiée possible. The inserted pour l'ordre donné à I has a long curved leader beneath it; that leader is not treated as another underline or as a strike. The short group after stricte contains dark joined s-like bodies and an i dot, leaving ssi/si unresolved. The two numbered conditions and the final stop are visible.

The first heading and Strat. fidèle each have one underline. The two small condition numbers after conditions are cramped; their order is not confidently distinguishable. The larger 3 and 4 in the continuation are clear. Fidèle appears again after the second heading. The final two abbreviated strat- groups have compressed endings that are not expanded. The connector between them has a definite leftward head and a rounded/closed right end, so a rightward head remains uncertain. The lower text sits immediately above the paper edge; no final stop is secure.
A thin numeral 3 has two curved lobes and no independent terminal stop. The pale line below it is not secure as an intentional underline; no hand attribution is made.

This narrow box clips almost all of the lower bodies and indices of the left formula, so those fragments are not completed here. The fourth-condition numeral is clear. The crossed X-like cluster and following quantifier are visible, but the cancelled subscript and much of the lower index line fall below the supplied boundary. The proposed i,j-in-I and j-less-than-i continuation is therefore retained locally uncertain in this box. No additional source crop was made.
